## service

One row per relying party: a service that uses CanadaLogin to sign its users in.
Services that run more than one application in CanadaLogin appear once here, not
once per application.

`Keywords`: Relying party, RP, service, application, department, operator, GC org

### Provenance

The list is maintained by hand in the
[CanadaLogin Relying Parties Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11czXAX6mTxZbbcH_XbFmI-TSoSTc2M5FXUp9teGw1D0/edit?gid=0#gid=0).
An AWS ETL reads the sheet once a day and writes a single Parquet file to S3. The
table is not partitioned and the file is overwritten in place, so this table
holds current state only and keeps no history.

* **Updated**: Daily
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://canadalogin-reporting-transformed/rp/service/`

### Fields

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rp_id` | `bigint` | Identifier for the relying party. Assigned by hand in the source sheet and stable across refreshes. Joins to `rp.alias.rp_id`. |
| `service_name_en` | `varchar` | English name of the service. Free text. |
| `service_name_fr` | `varchar` | French name of the service. Free text.  |
| `operator` | `varchar` | The organization that runs the service, typed by hand. Display only, see the note below. |
| `gc_orgid` | `bigint` | The `gc_orgID` of the operating organization, or `0` for entities that are not in the originating dataset. |
| `is_internal` | `boolean` | Is the service internal facing, rather than something the public signs in to? |
| `launch_date` | `varchar` | Approximate date the service launched to the public, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Stored as text. |
| `fetched_at` | `timestamp(3)` | When the ETL last read the source sheet. |

### Notes

**Group by `gc_orgid`, not `operator`.** `gc_orgid` comes from the
[GC Organization Names and Codes dataset](https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/57180b36-3428-4a7f-afe3-2161a6b44ec5)
on open.canada.ca, and IDs can be resolved to bilingual names through
[`cds-snc/gcorg-resolver`](https://github.com/cds-snc/gcorg-resolver). `operator`
is typed into the sheet by hand and does not follow the registry: some values are
full names (`Veterans Affairs Canada`), some are abbreviations (`PrairiesCan`),
and CanadaLogin's own services use `CanadaLogin`, which is not a GC organization
at all.

**`gc_orgid = 0` means not applicable, not missing.** It marks the services
CanadaLogin operates itself, which have no entry in the GC organization registry.
Excluding it removes CanadaLogin's own services, not bad data.

**`launch_date` is a string, so cast both sides when comparing.** Comparing it
against an R value that looks like an ISO date fails with
`TYPE_MISMATCH: Cannot apply operator: varchar = date`, because RAthena casts
ISO-format strings to a SQL `DATE` literal. Wrap both sides in `as.Date()`. The
same gotcha applies to `jira.psom.date` and `sre.uptime_summary.date`; see
[the notes page](notes.qmd).

**This is not a complete inventory of relying parties.** A service is added to the
sheet when it shows up in IBM Verify or the analytics data, so a service that is
live but has no traffic yet will be missing. Do not use `count(*)` here as the denominator for
"how many services use CanadaLogin".
